statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 19 sits in the low band, below the block threshold, while Stress 68 stays high on the rates and energy backdrop.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow danger window spans 12:30 to 14:30 UTC, covering the bundled US data block and the cash open, where the conditional readings of the cycle are highest.
headline: NQ recovers to 29,445.00 within 32 points of a five-hour-old session high without extending it; Tail holds at 19 while Stress eases to 68 as crude stabilises near $102.34
body:
The FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3-3/4 to 4 percent at 18:00 UTC on 16 September in a unanimous 12-0 vote, the first increase in three years, stating that economic activity is expanding at a solid pace while inflation remains elevated. Chair Warsh used the press conference to say inflation is too high and has been for too long. Goldman Sachs has since moved its next-hike expectation to the October meeting, published at 21:26 US Eastern on 16 September, and reporting overnight frames the decision as unlikely to be one-and-done.

Cash markets closed split on 16 September. The Nasdaq-100 finished at 28,945.06, up 0.02 percent, while the Dow fell about 1.6 percent and the S&P 500 about 0.4 percent. The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.01 percent against a 4.94 to 5.01 percent day range, the highest since 2007, and the H.15 release for 15 September shows the 2-year at 4.67 percent and the 10-year at 5.00 percent with the effective funds rate at 3.63 percent. VIX closed at 17.71, up 2.97 percent, after a 16.40 to 18.94 range.

Since the Globex reopen, NQ has traded a 29,247.75 to 29,477.00 range and is quoted at 29,445.00, up 0.64 percent, as of 03:15 UTC. The structure is the important part: the 29,477.00 high was set several hours ago and has not been extended since, the previous hour's fade to about 29,410 was bought back, and the 29,247.75 reopen low has now gone untested for five consecutive assessment hours. That is a range with functioning two-way trade rather than the repeated extension after failed retracements that the calibration treats as Tail evidence, so Tail is held at 19 in the low band. E-mini S&P futures corroborate the tone at 7,667.00, up 0.58 percent, inside a 7,617.50 to 7,669.75 range.

Cross-asset evidence is not aligned. WTI is quoted at 102.34 dollars, essentially unchanged overnight after a 3.2 percent drop to a 102.43 settlement, with Brent settling 2.7 percent lower at 105.83 dollars, as the United States said the damaged Saudi East-West pipeline outage would be measured in days while independent analysts warned the damage could keep it down for weeks. That unwinds part of a supply premium built during a month in which crude rallied more than 16 percent on Persian Gulf escalation, and the stabilisation is the main reason Stress eases a point to 68. Regional equity trade is two-way rather than directional: the Nikkei 225 is quoted at 63,966.87, up 0.07 percent, having faded roughly one percent from its 64,643.58 session high while US index futures held firm.

The scheduled path ahead is the 12:30 UTC block of initial jobless claims, August housing starts and building permits and the September Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index, the first labour and activity read priced against the new policy path, followed by the 13:30 UTC cash open and August pending home sales at 14:00 UTC. None of those has printed at assessment time, so they are carried as calendar checkpoints and conditional forecast readings, not as observed outcomes. The danger window is held narrow at 12:30 to 14:30 UTC for that reason.

Shared Finviz context was collected at 01:48 UTC, roughly 97 minutes before this assessment, and is therefore outside the freshness threshold and treated as stale; the collection was also partial, with the futures and calendar sections unavailable. Its breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections describe the latest cash session rather than live structure and are not used as current price-path evidence. The assessment relies on independently verified quotes and primary sources throughout.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding Claude clock-hours are available from published history and none has been restated with later information. The cycle opened in the low band at 14 to 16 with a normal dominant mode through the Asian and European sessions of 16 September, with no observed directional structure. It entered the watch band at 12:00 UTC with the US pre-market and held 20 to 22 through the early afternoon, reaching 24 in the 18:00 UTC statement hour. The single orange print came at 19:00 UTC, Tail 31 with a trend-down mode, during the press conference and the yield extension through 5 percent. It fell back to 20 within an hour and to 18 and 16 by 21:00 and 22:00 UTC as the post-event path proved orderly and retracements resumed, which is the pattern the calibration expects once price discovery completes. The overnight hours ran 18, 20, 20 and 19 as the Globex leg built and then stopped extending, with the watch-band prints resting on the untested reopen low rather than on any fresh amplifier. Stress stayed in the high band throughout, between 69 and 79, reflecting the rates and energy backdrop rather than index path behaviour.
outlookSummary: The forecast opens at 19 for the current hour, the only slot backed by observed price-path structure, then eases to an 18 plateau through the thin late-Asian and pre-European hours as the leg ages further out of its efficient window. It firms to 19 from the 07:00 UTC European cash open onward, where continental desks price the hike and a 5.01 percent ten-year, and holds there through the European morning. The 11:00 to 14:00 UTC slots carry the highest conditional readings at 20, 21, 23 and 22, spanning the bundled 12:30 UTC release block, the 13:30 UTC cash open and 14:00 UTC pending home sales; these are conditional event readings, not assertions that post-release continuation has been observed. From 15:00 UTC the path steps back to 20 and then 19 through the US afternoon on the usual midday liquidity decline, with a single 20 at 19:00 UTC for the power hour into the cash close. The final six slots decline through 18 and 17 into the maintenance break, the Globex reopen and the next Asian session. Stress traces the same shape from 68 now to a 67 overnight trough, 77 around the cash open and 65 at the horizon edge. Confidence decays from 85 to 62 purely with forecast horizon, since no live price path exists beyond the current hour.
